 Understanding Pandemic Related Academic Impact

Understanding pandemic related academic impact
• With the data Hawaii has from its state assessments, they are well
 positioned to investigate and address the academic impact of COVID-19.
• We are currently working with several states (including Hawaii, AZ, MA,
 RI, GA, CO) to support inferences from state assessments about the
 academic impact of the pandemic on students.
• Indiana, for example, passed legislation was passed requiring the DOE
 to produce annual reports that include analyses regarding pandemic
 related academic impact and recovery.
• Their ESSER state plan response details the learning loss report as
 evidence of compliance.
• A focal point of Center work over the last 6 months is to support such
 inferences.

Understanding pandemic related academic impact
• Hawaii is well positioned with it current assessments (SBAC and ACCESS) to
 derive academic impact data from those assessments.
• See the attached learning loss paper for more details.
• For example, Indiana will use its state summative test (ILEARN) and WIDA-
 ACCESS results to determine academic impact.
• The question is not so much how or if but whether Hawaii wants to pursue
 that direction.
• Potential Problems:
 • Low participation rates (< 50%) might cause issues with infernces.
 • Leadership not wanting to report/emphasize academic impact
 • Public reporting of data won’t align with academic impact use.
